subject: SLA remedies: escrowed funds, termination rights, and independent audit request
messages:
From: Samantha Ruiz <sruiz@nimblehealth.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Becker <tom.becker@procurement.nimblehealth.com>, legal@nimblehealth.com
Date: 2028-01-10T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: SLA remedies request — escrow + termination rights

Hi Olga / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the recent troubleshooting call. We appreciate the help, but NimbleHealth experienced three production-impacting latency incidents in the last four months (two partial region outages and one sustained 20% P99 degradation). Our executive team is now asking us to push harder on contractual remedies beyond recurring service credits.

High-level asks from Procurement & Legal:
- Escrowed funds equal to 6 months of committed monthly spend, to be held as a performance reserve if SLOs are repeatedly missed.
- Explicit termination right if we experience a second "major" outage (major = total customer-impacting downtime > 15 minutes or P99 > 800ms for >6 hours).
- A tiered liquidated damages schedule for severe incidents (we proposed 5%, 10%, 20% of monthly invoice depending on severity).
- Right to commission an independent uptime audit (once per 12 months) and access to incident telemetry and internal postmortems.

We are open to talking through definitions and cure periods, but these items are deal-breakers for the board unless we can agree on stronger protection than credits alone.

I'm attaching a short incident summary and would like to set a meeting with your legal and engineering leads this week. Proposed times: Wed 1/11 9–11am PT or Thu 1/12 2–4pm PT.

Thanks,
Samantha Ruiz
Director of Platform Ops
NimbleHealth

Attachments: incident_summary.pdf (4 pages)
From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Ruiz <sruiz@nimblehealth.com>, Tom Becker <tom.becker@procurement.nimblehealth.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-01-10T11:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA remedies request — escrow + termination rights

Samantha — thanks for the clear summary and for sharing the incident overview. I moved this to my calendar and looped in Aditya (engineering) and Karthik/Marissa from Legal so we can respond with specifics.

High level from our side: we absolutely prioritize reliability for customers like NimbleHealth and want to find a path to commerce that balances risk. Generally we push for credits + technical guardrails rather than large escrow/penalty provisions, but we recognize your board's concerns.

Questions before the meeting so we can come prepared:
- Can you confirm the total committed monthly spend you want the escrow sized against? (we need a hard number to model the exposure)
- For your proposed liquidated damages, are the percentages applied to a single-month invoice or to the committed MRR for the term?
- For an independent audit, would NimbleHealth cover the auditor fees and do you have preferred firms?

We attached the preliminary prod incident log we pulled so Aditya can comment before the call. Proposed next steps: short call to clarify definitions, then Legal exchange redlines. Wed 1/11 9:30am PT works for our team.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: NimbleHealth-prod-incident-log.csv (event timestamps, regions, P99 samples)
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, Samantha Ruiz <sruiz@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-01-11T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA remedies request — escrow + termination rights

Hi all — quick technical note ahead of our call. I dug through the logs attached by Olga and pulled additional traces. Short summary: 
- Incident 2027-10-14 (region-us-west-2): degraded P99 caused by an OOM event on a left-behind model shard during a background compaction job. We have a patch that isolates compaction and prevents preemption of inference workers.
- Incident 2027-11-28 (region-us-east-1): a transient networking flap in the cloud provider caused traffic skew and a token-migration delay; we added more aggressive backpressure and rebalanced KV-cache hot keys as a mitigation.
- Incident 2027-12-09 (global): internal autoscaling bug under bursty traffic produced a scale-down/scale-up oscillation; fix landed to the autoscaler and we're applying a safer cooldown window.

Mitigations in flight:
1) Cross-region failover playbook (ETA 8 weeks) to reduce single-region exposure.
2) New worker isolation in the runtime to avoid compaction-induced OOMs (patch rolling out in 2 weeks).
3) Expanded tracing and retained KV cache snapshots for 30 days for postmortem access.

We can provide an annotated incident timeline and an SLO measurement export for the last 12 months. These fixes significantly reduce the probability of repeat events, but I understand the need to capture contractual remedies while the mitigations are completing.

—Aditya
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Ruiz <sruiz@nimblehealth.com>, Tom Becker <tom.becker@procurement.nimblehealth.com>, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-01-12T15:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA remedies request — escrow + termination rights

Samantha / Tom — thanks for the candid ask and for joining earlier today. We discussed internally and drafted a counterproposal for the SLA language. Key commercial/legal points we propose (summary):

1) Performance holdback vs. escrow: rather than an on-chain/third-party escrow of 6 months' spend, we propose a contractual performance holdback equal to 4 months' average committed spend, held by Redwood and payable to NimbleHealth on qualifying breaches subject to a cure period and verification.
2) Termination trigger: termination right after three major outages in a rolling 12-month window (we propose three rather than two to allow for operational issues and cures).
3) Liquidated damages: agree a tiered schedule but capped at 50% of the monthly invoice per event and an aggregate cap across the term (we propose 3x monthly committed spend) to balance predictability.
4) Independent audit: we will agree to an independent uptime audit once per 12 months with auditor selection mutually agreed; NimbleHealth covers the auditor cost unless Redwood materially fails to provide requested telemetry.
5) Evidence & access: Redwood will provide incident telemetry exports, postmortems, and a SOC2 snapshot on request (redact customer PII as required).

I've attached a tracked redline of the SLA (redline_sla_NimbleHealth_v1.docx) with proposed wording and proposed cure periods (14 calendar days for operational fixes; 30 days for architectural remediation). Karthik and I are available to walk through the precise drafting.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redline_sla_NimbleHealth_v1.docx
From: Samantha Ruiz <sruiz@nimblehealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Becker <tom.becker@procurement.nimblehealth.com>, legal@nimblehealth.com
Date: 2028-01-13T08:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA remedies request — escrow + termination rights

Marissa / Olga — thanks for the thoughtful counter. A few points of pushback from NimbleHealth Legal/Procurement: 

- The board will not accept Redwood holding the funds unilaterally; they want a third-party escrow arrangement (neutral custodian) to avoid perceived conflicts of interest.
- We cannot accept three incidents as the termination threshold; our risk tolerance is lower given our clinical workflows — we insist on termination after two major incidents within 12 months.
- Aggregate caps need to be meaningful; 3x MRR feels low vs. the potential clinical impact and patient-safety risk. We propose a 6x MRR aggregate cap.

We are willing to accept the mutual auditor approach and to cover auditor fees. We will also agree to a reasonable cure period for operational fixes (14 days) but seek a shorter window (7 days) for critical security or data-integrity incidents.

I've attached the formal SLA request form that Legal has used historically; it lays out our non-negotiables and acceptable fallbacks.

Can we aim to resolve core commercial points (escrow amount, termination threshold, cap) by Fri 1/15 so procurement can proceed with the preferred VM sizing?

Thanks,
Samantha

Attachments: NimbleHealth-SLA-request-form.pdf
From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Ruiz <sruiz@nimblehealth.com>, Tom Becker <tom.becker@procurement.nimblehealth.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-01-16T16:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA remedies request — escrow + termination rights

Samantha — appreciate the clarity and the form you sent. We want to get this across the finish line in a way that preserves the relationship and addresses NimbleHealth's concerns. Proposed compromise for discussion with your board: 

- Escrow / holdback: 4 months' committed spend in a neutral third-party escrow (mutually appointed custodian). Funds are released per agreed triggers and subject to independent verification.
- Termination trigger: termination right after three major incidents OR two major incidents if one of the incidents involves data integrity or safety risk (we'll define the latter in the SLA).
- Aggregate damages cap: 4x MRR (increased from our prior 3x to show good faith; still provides Redwood predictability).
- Independent audit: mutually agreed auditor, NimbleHealth covers costs; Redwood will provide telemetry and SOC2 snapshot for audit review.

If this sounds workable, let's lock in a 30-minute legal call Tues 1/17 10am PT to finalize the redline and DocuSign flow. I'll have Marissa and Karthik on the call.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
